results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: Optional (if you need to discover URLs first) Prerequisite: Generate a deduped URL list using FIRECRAWL_MAP_MULTIPLE_URLS_BASED_ON_OPTIONS (seed crawl targets).
Required Step 1: Start parallel scraping using FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE (capture HTTP status + content and, if needed, outbound links for issue checks).
Required Step 2: Poll and retrieve completed results using FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET (review data[].metadata.statusCode plus any data[].metadata.error to flag page-level issues).
Required Step 3: Retrieve batch failures using FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET_ERRORS (include timeouts/blocked/robotsBlocked in the final issue report).
Optional Fallback (if a specific URL fails or batch scrape isn’t suitable) Fallback: Fetch that page using WEBSCRAPING_AI_GET_HTML (single-URL raw HTML check).
Optional Next Step (if you need broader coverage beyond the initial list) Next Step: Expand with FIRECRAWL_CRAWL and review failures using FIRECRAWL_CRAWL_GET_ERRORS.
Optional Next Step (if scraping large sets or using heavy formats) Next Step: Monitor quota/spend using FIRECRAWL_CREDIT_USAGE (avoid unexpected credit exhaustion).
known_pitfalls: [FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE] Returns a batch job id (and may include invalidURLs); page data is only available after FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET.
[FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET] Jobs can be "completed" while individual pages still show problems in data[].metadata.error or non-200 data[].metadata.statusCode—check per-page metadata.
[FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET] Large payloads when collecting content + links across many URLs can be difficult to handle in one response; plan to process incrementally/offline if needed.
[FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET_ERRORS] Can be empty even when some pages return non-200; use it for batch-level failures and rely on per-page statusCode for completeness.
[FIRECRAWL_CREDIT_USAGE] Credit-based quotas can be exhausted unexpectedly on large batches or rich formats; monitor before scaling up retries on blocked sites.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Parse a large FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET response to list non-200 pages and count status codes
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import json
r=json.load(open('/path/to/batch_scrape_get.json'))
d=r['results'][0]['response']['data']['data']
rows=[(x['metadata'].get('url'),x['metadata'].get('statusCode'),x['metadata'].get('error')) for x in d]
non200=[t for t in rows if isinstance(t[1],int) and t[1]!=200]
counts={}
for _,sc,_ in rows: counts[sc]=counts.get(sc,0)+1
(non200[:50],counts)
```

FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE.description: Tool to scrape multiple URLs in batch with concurrent processing. Use when you need to scrape multiple web pages efficiently with customizable formats and content filtering.

urls.description: The URLs to be scraped in batch. At least one URL is required.

proxy.description: Proxy type to use for requests.

maxAge.description: Cache validity period in milliseconds. Default is 2 days.

mobile.description: If true, emulate a mobile device when scraping. Defaults to false.

text.description: Text to be typed into an element.

type.description: The type of browser action to perform on the page before scraping. Supported actions: 'wait', 'click', 'screenshot', 'write', 'press', 'scroll'.

selector.description: CSS selector for the HTML element targeted by the action.

milliseconds.description: Duration in milliseconds for the action.

items.description: Action to perform on the page

actions.description: Browser actions to perform on each page before scraping.

formats.description: Desired output formats for the scraped content. Defaults to ['markdown'].

headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to send with each request.

waitFor.description: Delay in milliseconds before content retrieval. Useful for pages with dynamic content. Defaults to 0.

events.description: Event types to trigger webhook notifications.

headers.description: Custom headers to include in webhook requests.

metadata.description: Custom metadata to include in webhook payloads.

webhook.description: Webhook configuration for batch scrape notifications

blockAds.description: If true, block advertisements during scraping. Defaults to true.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to make the request from.

languages.description: List of preferred languages and locales for the request, in order of priority.

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically exclude from the output.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in the output.

storeInCache.description: If true, store scraped content in cache for future use. Defaults to true.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent scrape operations. Controls how many URLs are scraped simultaneously.

onlyMainContent.description: If true, extract only the main content, excluding headers, footers, navigation bars, and ads. Defaults to true.

ignoreInvalidURLs.description: If true, skip invalid URLs instead of failing the entire batch. Defaults to true.

zeroDataRetention.description: If true, do not retain any scraped data. Defaults to false.

removeBase64Images.description: If true, remove base64-encoded images from the scraped content. Defaults to true.

skipTlsVerification.description: If true, skip TLS certificate verification. Defaults to true.

FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET.description: Retrieves the current status and results of a batch scrape job using the job ID. Use this to check batch scrape progress and retrieve scraped data.

id.description: The ID of the batch scrape job. Must be a valid UUID format obtained when the batch scrape was initiated.

FIRECRAWL_BATCH_SCRAPE_GET_ERRORS.description: Tool to retrieve error details from a batch scrape job, including failed URLs and URLs blocked by robots.txt. Use when you need to debug or understand why certain pages failed to scrape in a batch operation.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the batch scrape job.

FIRECRAWL_MAP_MULTIPLE_URLS_BASED_ON_OPT.description: Maps a website by discovering URLs from a starting base URL, with options to customize the crawl via search query, subdomain inclusion, sitemap handling, and result limits; search effectiveness is site-dependent.

url.description: The starting website URL to map and discover links from. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL string (e.g., 'https://example.com'). Do NOT pass code snippets, SDK examples, or anything other than a plain URL.

limit.description: Maximum number of links to return. Defaults to 5000. Maximum allowed is 100000.

search.description: Optional search query to guide URL mapping, prioritizing or finding specific page types. 'Smart' search is limited to 1000 initial results in Alpha, but overall mapping can exceed this.

sitemap.description: Sitemap handling mode: 'skip' to exclude sitemaps, 'include' to use sitemaps with other discovery methods (default behavior), or 'only' to return only sitemap URLs.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. No timeout is applied by default.

location.description: Geographic settings for location-based request processing. Object with 'country' (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, e.g., 'US', 'DE', 'JP') and optionally 'languages' (array of language codes, e.g., ['en'], ['de', 'en']).

ignoreCache.description: If true, bypasses cached sitemap data. Useful when sitemaps have been recently updated. Sitemap data is cached for up to 7 days. Defaults to false.

includeSubdomains.description: If true, includes subdomains of the base URL in the mapping. E.g., if `url` is example.com, blog.example.com is mapped. Defaults to true.

ignoreQueryParameters.description: If true, excludes URLs with query parameters from results. Defaults to true.
